[round 1, 8a7daa17] Simulator side reproduced. 'INSERT INTO students VALUES (7,...,'Hull'),(8,'Hana','hana@example.com');' prints INSERT 0 2, stores NULL for Hana's city and ticks 'rows'. With a column list the same ragged VALUES gives 'INSERT has more target columns than expressions' rather than the VALUES-length ERROR. The server side comes from the cited VALUES documentation and was not executed. The ragged statement never completes Activity 2, because the column-list form errors. Rule applied to every adapter-fidelity defect in this module: escalate when the false Output cannot be made honest in scope; accept, with an in-loop mitigation and a recipe finding, when page-owned bytes can stop the defect from misleading the learner. Here they can, so this is accept. In-loop mitigation in src/insert-update-and-delete.topic.js: when an INSERT's VALUES rows differ in length (the outcome's st.rows keeps the raw lengths; verified [4,3] for this statement), do not tick 'rows', and add a note that every bracketed row needs the same number of values and a real PostgreSQL server rejects this statement. That changes display only; completion is unchanged. Record a recipe finding for the adapter's execInsert/parser in authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/engine.js to raise 'VALUES lists must all be the same length'. The 'INSERT 0 2' Output line stays wrong until then, so this also goes on the escalation list for tooling.

[round 1, 8a7daa17] Verified. Every unreadable statement, the empty-file prompt and every real subset limit reach the shell as kind 'limit' from the adapter's check() in authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/engine.js; I reproduced 'SELEC * FROM students;', a missing comma between two VALUES rows, a missing semicolon before a second SELECT and the untouched starter, all kind 'limit'. authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/controller.js relabels 'limit' as 'Not in this practice editor', and LIMITS item 4 in authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/build.mjs plus every page's Sources footer ('not as invalid PostgreSQL') say that label never means the SQL is wrong. The label is page-owned, so it is fixable in scope. Acceptable fix: in controller.js, wrap EDITOR.check (EDITOR is Object.create of the adapter) and re-kind problems by message into three classes. Real subset limits (WITH, psql meta-commands, CREATE TABLE and so on) keep 'Not in this practice editor'. Unreadable statements ('could not read the statement near', 'could not read one starting') get a learner label such as 'Check your SQL'. The empty-file prompt gets its own neutral label. Message matching is feasible: I checked that real limits carry their own messages ('WITH queries are outside this practice editor', 'CREATE is not available here', 'Transactions are outside this practice editor', 'COPY runs on the database server', and the psql meta-command text), distinct from the unreadable-statement messages. Never use the adapter's own 'Lesson check' (B4), and never use kind 'hint', because the shell blocks Run only on non-hint problems. Run gating, the 'limit' notRun status and onSqlRun's 'did not use up a try' path must stay exactly as they are (E2 is pending). Reword LIMITS item 4 and the footer sentence in each src/<topic>.body.html and artifact.md to match. The minimum acceptable fix, if message matching seems too brittle, is one neutral label covering both cases, with LIMITS and footer sentences that no longer say the SQL is fine. Shell wording stays a recipe finding. On this page, the missing comma between the two bracketed rows (Activity 2's main slip) reproduces as kind 'limit' at Ln 3 near "(". The critic grades the same root cause high here and medium on the other pages; the decision and the fix are the same.

[round 1, 8a7daa17] Verified strings. The authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/build.mjs badge reads 'Practice editor: follows PostgreSQL on this page's sample tables' and the status span reads 'SQL practice editor'. In authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/controller.js, EDITOR.language='PostgreSQL server' feeds the shell's Output header '(lesson simulator, not real PostgreSQL server)', while SQLCHK.explain says 'PostgreSQL cannot tell which one you mean' / 'PostgreSQL would stop with the ERROR'. The shell's empty Problems text is 'No problems found by the lesson checker', which also uses B4 grader vocabulary. C2 F5 says a page never says both 'not real' and 'PostgreSQL rejected'. In-loop fix, page-owned bytes only: use one name ('practice editor') in the build.mjs badge and status span, choose EDITOR.language so the shell header reads consistently with it, and word the explain lines as what 'a real PostgreSQL server' would report. The shell's 'lesson simulator, not real' prefix and its 'No problems found by the lesson checker' sentence are engine.js shell bytes: record a recipe finding.

[round 1, 8a7daa17] Verified. CONF in authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/build.mjs prints Low / Medium / High, but DESIGN.md (Assessment: options, confidence, feedback) sets "Guessing", "Fairly sure", "Certain". In authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/controller.js, checkPredict writes 'Your guess was not this time', and summarize() joins open activities as 'Activity '+open.join(' and '), which gives 'Activity 2 and 3 and 4 are'. Fix, wording only: in CONF, use the DESIGN.md labels (the radio values low/medium/high may stay). calibration() echoes the raw value ('Your confidence: medium'), so map it to the shown label. Write 'Your guess was not right this time', and join a list as 'Activities 2, 3 and 4 are' (singular 'Activity 2 is').

[round 1, 8a7daa17] Reproduced at 570x1000 under file:// and over http://127.0.0.1: scrollY 157, exactly the top of #activity-1. At 1280 px it is 121 on inner-and-left-joins and 0 where the document fits. Cause confirmed: with history.replaceState stubbed out, scrollY stays 0. The last line of authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/controller.js calls go(...,'replace'), whose history.replaceState(#activity-1) runs during parsing. It does not throw, and the browser's load-time scroll-to-fragment then scrolls to #activity-1, so F1 fails on the narrow frame (G7). Fix in controller.js: on first load with no #activity-N in the URL, do not write a hash (call go with no history mode), or write it after load and keep scroll at 0. Keep the hash behaviour for later navigation. Measured in headless Chromium only; check the platform embed after the fix.

[round 3, 02be5a14] Verified at 02be5a14 by parsing the bank with authoring/tools/gift/validate.mjs parseGift and comparing option answer lengths (correct vs longest distractor): 'o1 why name the columns' 84 vs 41; 'o3 RETURNING after UPDATE' 40 vs 29. Also, though not cited, 'o1 two rows, named columns' 62 vs 60 (a negligible margin). Is the remedy available on this branch? No. In authoring/tests/gift-answer-order.test.mjs, the test 'topic GIFT banks keep the semantics they had before the answer-order permutation' parses each bank at baseline f2647727 (present in this clone, so the test is not skipped). For every baseline question, baselineProblems() reports '<title> changed' when semanticDigest differs. In authoring/tools/gift/answer-order.mjs, semanticDigest hashes the category, the title, the stem and each option's [correct, answer, feedback] text. So any wording change that lengthens a distractor or trims a correct option changes the digest and fails npm test. This bank exists at the baseline. Its bytes at 02be5a14 are identical to origin/main (sha256 compared), so the length cue is pre-existing on main and not introduced by this branch's content. The only edit the test allows is appending new questions with new titles. That cannot remove the cue from the existing items, so it is not a fix. Decision: escalate, not reject, because the finding is true and fails C2 D7 ('the correct option is not the longest') and DESIGN.md Assessment. It cannot be accepted on this branch, because the only remedy needs a test or tooling change, which the branch may not make. The captain or tooling owner must decide whether to refresh the frozen baseline for reviewed wording-only length rebalancing, or to add a reviewed-exception mechanism. That would be a tooling branch, followed by a course or module branch that rebalances these items with answer-order.mjs, keeping each option's meaning and the keyed answer.
